## What Drives Painting Costs in Melbourne

Jetblack Painting quotes after seeing the property rather than publishing a rate per square metre, because the factors below move the price far more than floor area does. Written quotes are free, itemised, and typically provided within 24–48 hours.

### Interior painting
- **Wall and ceiling condition** — cracked cornices, water stains, old wallpaper and years of patch repairs need significant preparation before a topcoat goes on. This usually matters more than room count.
- **Colour change** — going dark to light, or covering a strong existing colour, often needs a tinted primer or an extra coat.
- **Ceiling height and access** — standard 2.4m ceilings are straightforward; raked ceilings, stairwells and double-height living areas need scaffolding or specialised access.
- **Finish level** — a washable low-sheen in a high-traffic hallway costs more to supply than a basic flat finish, and lasts considerably longer.

### Exterior painting
- Substrate (weatherboard, render, brick), number of storeys, access, and the amount of preparation the surface needs. Pressure washing, sanding, filling and priming are included in every quote.

### Roof painting
- Roof size, pitch, substrate and condition. Cracked or slipped tiles, failed ridge capping and rusted sheeting are repairs that must happen before coating. A sound roof properly coated has its life extended by 10–15 years.

### Kitchen cabinet resurfacing
- Door and drawer count, colour change, substrate condition, hardware reuse and gloss level. Resurfacing typically costs 30–50% less than a full kitchen renovation because the layout, carcasses and benchtops stay in place. Most kitchens take 5–10 days from first preparation to refitting.

### Commercial and body corporate
- Scope, area, access equipment, and whether work is staged around trading hours or residents. Detailed written scopes are provided for committee approval.

**For a price, call Jimmy on 0432 077 782 or email jimmy@jetblackpainting.com. Site visits and written quotes are free.**

Roof painting is quoted on roof size, pitch, substrate and condition, and whether repairs are needed first. Cracked or slipped tiles, failed ridge capping and rusted sheeting have to be fixed before a coating goes on. Every roof painting quote includes pressure cleaning, crack repair, priming and quality roof coatings.

**How much does commercial painting cost?**

**Do I have to pay the full amount upfront?**
No. A reasonable deposit to secure materials and a start date is standard practice, with the balance tied to job progress or completion rather than paid entirely in advance. Be cautious of any painter asking for full payment before work starts.

### Timeline Questions

**How long does a house painting job take?**
Most interior repaints take a few days to a week depending on the size of the home, access, and the preparation required — a single room is usually a day or two. Exterior repaints take a few days depending on access, prep and weather. Kitchen cabinet resurfacing takes 5–10 days from first preparation to refitting the doors. Roof painting takes 1–3 days depending on roof size and pitch.

**How long does interior painting take?**
Most interior painting projects take 3–7 days depending on the size and complexity. A single room typically takes 1–2 days. A full 3-bedroom home typically takes 3–5 days. A detailed timeline is provided during your free quote.

**How long does exterior painting take?**
Exterior painting typically takes 2–4 days depending on home size, surface condition, weather, and access. Surface preparation (pressure washing, sanding, repairs) often takes as long as the painting itself — all included in your quote.

**What's the best time of year to paint in Melbourne?**
Exterior painting is best done between October and April when conditions are drier and warmer. Avoid days below 10°C or above 35°C, and high-humidity days, since they affect how paint cures. Interior painting can be done year-round.

### Quality & Guarantee Questions

**What guarantee does Jetblack Painting offer?**
Every job is backed by a 5-year written workmanship guarantee. If anything related to Jetblack Painting's workmanship fails within 5 years, they return to fix it at no cost. This covers peeling, flaking, poor adhesion, and paint defects.

**What paint brands does Jetblack Painting use?**
Jetblack Painting uses premium Australian paint brands — primarily Dulux and Taubmans — selecting the right product for each surface and environment. For coastal homes, products rated for salt air and UV resistance are used. Exact product recommendations are provided in your quote.

**How do you protect coastal homes from salt air damage?**
Salt air deposits on surfaces, breaks down paint adhesion and accelerates rust on metal trim — causing paint to fail in 2–3 years if poorly prepared. Jetblack Painting counters this with thorough salt-air washing, flexible primers rated for coastal use, and premium topcoats formulated for salt air exposure.

**What does exterior painting preparation include?**
Jetblack Painting's exterior preparation includes: pressure washing (and salt washing for coastal homes), scraping and sanding loose or failing paint, filling cracks and gaps, caulking around windows and trim, patching damaged render or weatherboard, priming bare areas, and masking fixtures and landscaping.

**Can you paint two-storey homes or properties with difficult access?**
Yes. Single-storey homes with clear ground access are straightforward; two-storey homes, steep gables, raked ceilings, stairwells and sloped blocks are assessed for scaffolding or elevated access equipment as part of the quote, so the access requirement and any added cost is clear upfront rather than a surprise.

### Paint Problem Diagnosis

**Why is my paint peeling or flaking off?**
Peeling almost always means the coating never bonded properly to what was underneath it. The usual causes are moisture getting behind the film, painting over a chalky or glossy surface without sanding and priming, or applying a coating incompatible with the one below it. Peeling that starts at window sills, door frames and the bottom of weatherboards points to water; peeling in broad sheets across a wall points to preparation. Repainting over it will not fix it — the failing layer has to come back to a sound edge first, and the underlying moisture path found and stopped.

**Why is my paint bubbling or blistering?**
Blisters are the coating lifting away from the surface, usually because moisture or solvent is trapped underneath. The three common causes in Melbourne homes are painting over a damp substrate, painting in direct sun or high heat so the surface skins over before the layer beneath can release, and moisture pushing out from inside the wall — a leak, rising damp or an unventilated bathroom. Small blisters that expose bare substrate when opened mean the moisture came from behind; blisters that reveal another paint layer mean it was a topcoat adhesion problem.

**What is chalking, and does it mean I need to repaint?**
Chalking is the powdery residue that comes off on your hand when you rub a sun-facing wall. It is UV breaking down the binder in the paint, and it is a normal end-of-life signal rather than a defect. It matters at repaint time because a new coating applied over chalk will bond to loose powder instead of the wall and fail early. The chalk has to be washed off completely and the surface sealed before anything new goes on. Heavy chalking on the north and west elevations while the south wall still looks sound is the usual pattern.

**Do I need to treat mould before painting over it?**
Yes, and painting over it without treating it is the single most common mistake. Mould is a living growth, not a stain — a coating laid over it will be pushed through within months, and the new paint gives it a moisture-holding surface to spread on. The growth has to be killed, physically removed, the surface allowed to dry, and the moisture source addressed, before any primer goes on. Bathrooms, laundries, south-facing bedroom walls and window reveals are where it recurs. Anti-mould additives in the topcoat help afterwards but do not substitute for treating it first.

**Does my Melbourne home have lead paint?**
If it was built before 1970, assume yes until tested. Lead was used in Australian household paint until then, so original coatings on Victorian, Edwardian, interwar and early post-war homes commonly contain it — typically buried under later layers on window sashes, door frames, skirtings and external weatherboards. Intact, sound paint is not the hazard. Disturbing it is. Dry sanding or power-sanding an old coating turns it into lead dust through the house, which is the real risk to children and pets. Testing before disturbing original surfaces, working wet, containing the area and disposing of the waste properly is the correct approach on any pre-1970 property.

**Can I paint over wallpaper?**
Sometimes, but it is usually the wrong call. If the paper is thoroughly stuck down with no lifting seams or bubbles, it can be sealed and painted. In practice most older wallpaper has loose edges, and the moisture in the paint releases the adhesive so seams lift and telegraph through the finish within weeks. Vinyl and washable papers are worse again because coatings will not key to them. Removing the paper and making the wall good underneath gives a result that lasts, and it is usually the cheaper decision once the cost of redoing a failed job is counted.

### Living Through the Job

**Do I need to move my furniture before the painters arrive?**
No. Furniture is moved to the centre of the room and covered, and floors are protected before any work starts. Clearing small items, valuables, wall hangings and the contents of built-in robes ahead of time speeds things up and is worth doing, but the heavy lifting is part of the job rather than something to arrange yourself.

**Can I stay in the house while it is being painted?**
Yes, in almost all cases. Interior work is staged room by room so the house stays liveable, and modern low-VOC paints mean rooms are usable again quickly rather than needing to be aired out for days. Kitchens and bathrooms are planned around so you are not without them. If someone in the house has a respiratory condition or there is a newborn, say so at the quote and the sequencing can be planned around it.

**Do painters clean up afterwards?**
Yes. Drop sheets, masking and debris are removed, furniture is returned to position, and surfaces are left clean at the end of the job. A final walk-through of every surface happens with you before sign-off, so anything you are not happy with is identified and corrected before the crew leaves rather than after.

**What preparation is actually included in the quote?**
All of it — preparation is not an optional line item. Every quote itemises the washing, scraping, sanding, filling, caulking, patching and priming needed for that specific property, so you can see what you are paying for rather than being given a single lump sum. Preparation frequently takes as long as the painting itself, and it is the part that determines whether the finish lasts five years or two.
